reading.body:
Kansas has three catalogued data center facilities and a recorded total capacity of zero megawatts, meaning the power draw of these sites is either undisclosed or not yet collected.

The three facilities span two distinct geographies: one site in Hays, near the center of the state, and two in the Kansas City suburbs of Lenexa and Olathe. That western site is notably isolated from major metro infrastructure, while the two Johnson County facilities sit within a regional cluster that crosses into Missouri. None of the three entries carry a megawatt figure, so no comparison of scale between them is possible from this data alone.

For AI specifically, capacity in watts is the number that determines whether a facility can support GPU-dense workloads. Without it, a facility count tells you only that buildings exist, not whether they represent meaningful compute infrastructure. This record documents presence but not power, and readers should treat it as a geographic starting point rather than a capacity assessment.
